Subject: Implementation: Vento Health private deployment — network runbook & next steps

Hi Asha / Mark —

Great to meet earlier this week. Per our kickoff, I'm consolidating the immediate network and implementation asks so we can lock a technical working session and hand off to our delivery team. High-level items we need to align on: 

- VPC connectivity model: VPC peering vs PrivateLink (we typically recommend PrivateLink for minimal blast radius, but peering can be lower latency).
- IP addressing: CIDR blocks, NAT/egress constraints, and whether the Vento infra team can allocate an endpoint IP range for private endpoints.
- On-prem package: scope for the on-prem artifact (air-gapped bundle) and install window for your infra team.
- TLS & termination: where TLS is terminated (customer LB, Redwood-managed endpoint, or mutual TLS).
- Firewall and routing runbook: sample firewall rules and ports we'll need opened for probes, RPC, and health-checks.

I've attached a short private-deploy-checklist with the items we usually collect ahead of the technical session. Can you send the network inventory and the contact for your netops (if different from Mark) so Dylan and Lauren can schedule a detailed working session next week?

Proposed next steps:
1) Vento shares network inventory and preferred connectivity window (target by 2026-04-10).
2) Schedule 90-minute technical working session with your netops + Akira Networks (if they're supporting on-prem connectivity).
3) Delivery team (Dylan/Dev) produce a runbook and firewall template within 3 business days of the session.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite once we have a preferred day.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Mark / Asha —

Quick technical notes from our side ahead of the session:

- PrivateLink (AWS VPC Endpoint Services) is our preferred path for private-hosted customers when you need strict egress control and no cross-account VPC peering. It preserves your central NAT behavior.
- If you'd prefer VPC peering, we'll need to coordinate routing priorities and ensure there are no overlapping CIDRs; peering may require additional firewall/NAT rules.
- For on-prem connectivity (via Akira), we need the following:
  - BGP ASN (if using BGP) and the expected public IPs for the tunnel
  - Firewall allowlist entries (see sample below)
  - Health-check IPs (we use a small set of stable IPs for probes)

Sample firewall / egress requirements (high level):
- Outbound TCP: 443 to 34.120.0.0/16 (Redwood managed endpoints)
- Outbound TCP: 443 to private endpoint IPs we create in your VPC (will provide exact IPs post-provisioning)
- Inbound: minimal — only from your management jump hosts for admin

I've attached our internal VPC peering guide and a short template we use for firewall rules. During the session we can lock a preferred approach and I'll turn that into a draft runbook.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-vpc-peering-guide.md (text/markdown)

Hi all —

Thanks for the details. To keep the delivery cadence tight, here's a proposed minimal runbook we'll finalize after the technical session: 

1) Provisioning (Day 0)
  - Redwood requests creation of a /28 for PrivateLink endpoints in your customer VPC (we will consume 2 IPs).
  - Provide BGP ASN and public IPs for Akira tunnel.

2) Firewall template (for change control)
  - Allow outbound TCP/443 to Redwood probe IPs: 34.120.16.10, 34.120.16.11
  - Allow outbound TCP/443 to PrivateLink endpoint IPs (exacts post-provisioning)
  - Allow TCP/22 only from your admin jump hosts to the on-prem admin node (if using on-prem package)

3) On-prem agent install (if chosen)
  - Pre-stage air-gapped bundle on an isolated jump host
  - Run health-check script and confirm outbound heartbeats to provided probe IPs

4) Compliance & evidence
  - Connor will collect SOC2 attestation and any required subprocessor list.
  - We will provide audit log location and retention policy for your records.

Proposed dates: technical working session on 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC (90 mins). If that works, we'll send a calendar invite. After the session we aim to deliver a complete runbook within 3 business days.

Attachments: onprem-deploy-runbook-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks,
Dev Patel
